name: Rocket UniData / UniVerse
tagline: Rocket's Pick-style MultiValue databases, powering thousands of vertical business applications.
description: UniVerse and UniData are the two MultiValue (Pick-family) databases sold together as Rocket U2. Records are dynamic arrays whose fields can hold multiple values and sub-values, described by optional dictionaries, so one record can hold an order with all its lines; applications are written in a BASIC dialect with English-like query languages (RetrieVe/UniQuery) and an SQL layer. Rocket bought U2 from IBM in 2009 and keeps both lines current: UniVerse 14.2.1 shipped in November 2025 with an optional recoverable file system, and UniData 8.3.2 in 2024. Expect to find them inside long-lived ERP, healthcare, banking and distribution packages rather than in new builds.

pricing.notes: Commercial per-user licensing, often via application resellers; free personal editions for learning.

scale.notes: Single-server engines; U2 Data Replication provides hot standby and DR.

strengths: Nested multi-value records model orders, invoices and patient charts without join tables
Embedded Python and REST services help modernise BASIC applications
Very fast keyed access on hashed files
Active vendor releases from Rocket for both UniVerse and UniData
weaknesses: Niche skills; Pick BASIC developers are increasingly rare
SQL layer is an afterthought compared with the native query languages
No horizontal scaling; HA relies on replication add-ons
useCases: Running vertical ERP, distribution and healthcare packages built on U2
Modernising Pick applications behind REST and .NET
notIdealFor: Analytics without exporting to SQL systems
